newsitem.title: USA: BP/Sterling Texas methanol plant in force majeure.
newsitem.headline: BP/Sterling Texas methanol plant in force majeure.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc unit BP Chemicals has declared force majeure on all the output at its 10,000 barrel per day methanol plant in Texas City because of a compressor problem at the plant, the company said Friday.
Methanol business manager Bob Niedzielski said the plant was shut down on Thursday, and because of the tight methanol market the company could not meet its scheduled commitments.
He said the plant will be down 10 to 12 days.
"We did not have enough inventories to meet our scheduled commitments and could not borrow product from other producers so far," said Niedzielski.
"Everyone in this industry has very little supply," he added.
According to traders, methanol prices have strengthened since Thursday, rising to as much as 85.00 cents a gallon on Friday from about 60.00 cents before the news.
"It's definitely had an affect," said one methanol player.
Some players said prices of MTBE, which is made in part with methanol, rose to 79.00 cents a gallon from about 78.00 cents.
The plant, which began production in May 1995, is a joint venture with Sterling Chemicals Inc.
"I still hope to meet all my commitments by March but poeple will get their product in the second half of March instead of the first half," said Niedzielski.
He added that he had a 10,000 barrel commitment to meet on Sunday, and a 20,000 barrel one to meet on Tuesday. ((New York Energy Desk 212 859-1631))
